Bench-ready protocol for measuring maximum water holding capacity (WHC) of sieved soil by gravity drainage through pre-weighed filter paper, drying the same filter-paper-plus-soil system, and calculating WHC by mass balance.

<div class="facts">
<div class="fact"><strong>System</strong><span>Tin + filter + soil</span></div>
<div class="fact"><strong>Drainage</strong><span>8-12 h</span></div>
<div class="fact"><strong>Drying</strong><span>105 deg C</span></div>
<div class="fact"><strong>Output</strong><span id="summaryWhc">WHC g/g</span></div>
</div>

---

## Before Starting

::: {.alert .alert-info role="alert"}
**Why measure WHC**

Gravity-drainage WHC reflects the water a sieved soil retains after overnight gravitational drainage. It is useful for setting incubation moisture as a consistent percentage of WHC across soils with different texture and organic matter.

:::
::: {.alert .alert-success role="alert"}
**Mass-balance setup**

Pre-weigh the filter paper and tin. After drainage, weigh the tin + filter paper + wet soil together, then dry that same system. This avoids scraping wet soil from the filter paper and keeps all soil in the measured system.

:::
::: {.alert .alert-warning role="alert"}
**Consistency matters**

Apply a WHC value only to soil prepared the same way. Sieving, drying, and pre-incubation handling can change the measured value.

:::
---

## Materials

- Analytical balance, 0.01 g resolution or better
- Glass or plastic funnel, 60-100 mm diameter
- Whatman No. 40 filter paper, or equivalent ashless medium-flow filter paper
- Ring stand and funnel support
- Collection vessel, such as beaker or graduated cylinder
- DI water or distilled water
- 2 mm sieve
- Drying oven set to 105 deg C
- Aluminum weighing tins or drying dishes
- Desiccator
- Timer
- Parafilm or clean loose cover

---

## WHC Calculator

<div class="calculator-controls">
<div class="control">
<label for="filterMassInput">Filter paper empty mass, W_filter (g)</label>
<input id="filterMassInput" type="number" min="0" step="0.0001" value="0.80">
</div>
<div class="control">
<label for="tinMassInput">Tin empty mass, W_tin (g)</label>
<input id="tinMassInput" type="number" min="0" step="0.0001" value="2.50">
</div>
<div class="control">
<label for="wetTotalInput">Tin + filter + wet soil, W_wet_total (g)</label>
<input id="wetTotalInput" type="number" min="0.01" step="0.01" value="71.72">
</div>
<div class="control">
<label for="dryTotalInput">Tin + filter + dry soil, W_dry_total (g)</label>
<input id="dryTotalInput" type="number" min="0.01" step="0.01" value="53.15">
</div>
</div>

| Calculation | Value |
|---|---:|
| Dry soil mass, W_soil,dry | <span id="drySoilMass">49.85 g</span> |
| Wet soil mass, W_soil,wet | <span id="wetSoilMass">68.42 g</span> |
| Water retained after drainage | <span id="waterRetained">18.57 g</span> |
| WHC | <span id="whcValue">0.373 g water/g dry soil</span> |
| Gravimetric water content | <span id="gravWaterContent">37.3%</span> |

::: {.alert .alert-warning role="alert"}
**Check mass entries**

W_wet_total should be greater than W_dry_total, and both totals should be greater than W_tin + W_filter. If not, recheck labels, tare values, or sample transfer.

:::
---

## Part A: Prepare Soil and Funnel

*~15-30 min*

<ul class="checklist">
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Sieve field-moist or air-dried soil through a 2 mm sieve.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Prepare one replicate per sample type. Run duplicates if sample variability is unknown.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>With the balance calibrated and zero-tared, weigh the dry filter paper and record empty filter mass as <code>W_filter</code>.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Weigh the empty labeled drying tin and record tin mass as <code>W_tin</code>.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Fold the pre-weighed Whatman No. 40 filter paper into a cone and seat it firmly in the funnel with no wall gaps.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Wet the filter paper with a small volume of DI water to seal it against the funnel wall.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Allow excess water to drain completely before adding soil.</span></li>
</ul>

---

## Part B: Saturate Soil

*~10-20 min*

<ul class="checklist">
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Weigh the chosen starting mass of sieved soil into the prepared funnel.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Slowly add DI water in small increments across the soil surface.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Stop when the soil is visibly saturated and water just begins to emerge from the funnel tip.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>For mineral soils, expect roughly 50-80 mL water, but use visible saturation rather than a fixed volume.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Add water gradually to avoid channeling through the soil.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Cover the funnel loosely with Parafilm or a clean cap to limit evaporation.</span></li>
</ul>

---

## Part C: Drain Overnight

*8-12 h elapsed*

<ul class="checklist">
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Allow the soil to drain at room temperature for at least 8 h, recording the drainage start and end time when the funnel is removed from the stand. Overnight drainage is preferred.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Do not disturb the funnel during drainage.</span></li>
</ul>

---

## Part D: Weigh Wet Soil System

*~10-20 min*

<ul class="checklist">
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>After drainage, transfer the wet filter paper and all retained wet soil together into the pre-weighed tin.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Weigh the tin + filter paper + wet soil together and record as <code>W_wet_total</code>.</span></li>
</ul>

---

## Part E: Determine Oven-Dry Mass

*24 h or until stable*

<ul class="checklist">
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Dry the same tin + filter paper + soil system at 105 deg C for at least 24 h.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Continue drying until mass is stable, such as two consecutive readings differing by less than 0.01 g.</span></li>
  <li><input type="checkbox"><span>Cool in a desiccator for 20-30 min, then weigh and record tin + filter paper + dry soil as <code>W_dry_total</code>.</span></li>
</ul>

---

## Calculation Notes

```text
W_soil,dry = W_dry_total - W_tin - W_filter

W_soil,wet = W_wet_total - W_tin - W_filter

Water retained = W_soil,wet - W_soil,dry

WHC (g water / g dry soil) = Water retained / W_soil,dry
```

This mass-balance approach avoids scraping soil from the filter paper. Any soil that remains attached to the filter paper is included in both the wet and dry total masses.

**Example**

| Parameter | Value |
|---|---:|
| W_filter | 0.80 g |
| W_tin | 2.50 g |
| W_wet_total | 71.72 g |
| W_dry_total | 53.15 g |
| W_soil,wet | 71.72 - 2.50 - 0.80 = 68.42 g |
| W_soil,dry | 53.15 - 2.50 - 0.80 = 49.85 g |
| WHC | (68.42 - 49.85) / 49.85 = 0.373 g/g |

## Stop Points

::: {.alert .alert-danger role="alert"}
**Stop and ask before**

- Using the WHC value for a soil batch that was sieved, dried, or handled differently.
- Continuing if soil does not drain within 12 h.
- Accepting duplicate WHC values that differ by more than 15% for the same soil.
- Separating wet soil from the filter paper before weighing, because soil stuck to the filter paper will break mass balance.
- Using a different filter paper type or funnel geometry without noting the change.

:::
---

## References

- Protocols.io. Determination of Water Holding Capacity (WHC) of Soil Samples. https://www.protocols.io/view/determination-of-water-holding-capacity-whc-of-soi-f9tpbr6mp.html
- Franzluebbers AJ. 2020. Holding water with capacity to target porosity. *Agricultural & Environmental Letters* 5:e20029.
- Slatyer RO, McIlroy IC. 1961. *Practical Microclimatology*. CSIRO, Melbourne.

<script>
(function () {
  const filterMassInput = document.getElementById("filterMassInput");
  const tinMassInput = document.getElementById("tinMassInput");
  const wetTotalInput = document.getElementById("wetTotalInput");
  const dryTotalInput = document.getElementById("dryTotalInput");
  const labNotes = document.getElementById("labNotes");
  const clearNotes = document.getElementById("clearNotes");
  const notesStatus = document.getElementById("notesStatus");
  const notesStorageKey = "soil-whc-gravity-drainage-notes";

  function el(id) { return document.getElementById(id); }
  function setText(id, text) { const node = el(id); if (node) node.textContent = text; }
  function value(input, fallback, min) {
    const parsed = parseFloat(input.value);
    return Math.max(min, Number.isFinite(parsed) ? parsed : fallback);
  }
  function fmtMass(v) {
    return (Number.isInteger(v) ? v : v.toFixed(2)) + " g";
  }
  function fmtRatio(v) {
    return (Number.isFinite(v) ? v.toFixed(3) : "Check") + " g/g";
  }

  function updateWhc() {
    const filter = value(filterMassInput, 0.8, 0);
    const tin = value(tinMassInput, 2.5, 0);
    const wetTotal = value(wetTotalInput, 71.72, 0.01);
    const dryTotal = value(dryTotalInput, 53.15, 0.01);
    const tare = filter + tin;
    const wetSoil = wetTotal - tare;
    const drySoil = dryTotal - tare;
    const retained = wetSoil - drySoil;
    const whc = drySoil > 0 ? retained / drySoil : NaN;
    const waterPct = Number.isFinite(whc) ? whc * 100 : NaN;

    setText("summaryWhc", Number.isFinite(whc) ? whc.toFixed(3) + " g/g" : "Check");
    setText("drySoilMass", fmtMass(drySoil));
    setText("wetSoilMass", fmtMass(wetSoil));
    setText("waterRetained", fmtMass(retained));
    setText("whcValue", fmtRatio(whc) + " dry soil");
    setText("gravWaterContent", Number.isFinite(waterPct) ? waterPct.toFixed(1) + "%" : "Check");
    setText("recordFilterMass", fmtMass(filter));
    setText("recordTinMass", fmtMass(tin));
    setText("recordWetTotal", fmtMass(wetTotal));
    setText("recordDryTotal", fmtMass(dryTotal));
    setText("recordWetSoil", fmtMass(wetSoil));
    setText("recordDrySoil", fmtMass(drySoil));
    setText("recordWhc", fmtRatio(whc));
  }

  function initNotes() {
    try { labNotes.value = localStorage.getItem(notesStorageKey) || ""; } catch (e) {}
    labNotes.addEventListener("input", function () {
      try {
        localStorage.setItem(notesStorageKey, labNotes.value);
        notesStatus.textContent = "Saved locally in this browser.";
      } catch (e) {
        notesStatus.textContent = "Could not save notes.";
      }
    });
    clearNotes.addEventListener("click", function () {
      labNotes.value = "";
      try {
        localStorage.removeItem(notesStorageKey);
        notesStatus.textContent = "Notes cleared.";
      } catch (e) {}
    });
  }

  [filterMassInput, tinMassInput, wetTotalInput, dryTotalInput].forEach(function (input) {
    input.addEventListener("input", updateWhc);
  });

  initNotes();
  updateWhc();
})();
</script>
